title: Refuse or warn on a blocked item at wave start

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Parity row 3.7 and gap 17 (docs/orchestrator-parity.md in the s165 worktree). The outer session orders a wave by dependencies. ork asks `slicer plan-parallel` for suggested waves (`wave.suggest`, `internal/daemon/reads.go:55-63`), but `startWave` admits whatever the caller names, in the order given. It checks the engine-conflict guard and then the spec gate (`internal/daemon/runs.go:597-645`); no code there reads slicer's dependency state (searched `internal/daemon` for `blocked` and `deps`: only `wave.overlap` uses `slicer deps --overlap`). In Waves the owner can tick a wave-2 item with its wave-1 dependency, and `ork wave start PROJECT ID...` takes any ids, so an item whose dependency is not done can start (`internal/cli/wave.go:60-175`).

Slicer already answers this: `slicer deps ID --json --lean` returns `blocked_by`, the dependencies not in a satisfying status plus any open slivers (`slicer/src/slicer/cli.py:2292-2312`, `slicer/src/slicer/graph.py:83-107`). A dependency in the same wave is still not done, so it blocks. ork calls the command and does not recompute the graph.

Owner decision 2026-10-29 (orchestrator-parity.md, Owner decisions): every gap is a v1.0 slice. The wording "refuse or warn" is the analysis's; the safest default below is to refuse (Open 1).

Design (*proposed*): a new read `slicercli.Client.ItemDeps(root, id)` over `slicer deps ID --json --lean`. A shared daemon check `blockedItems(ctx, proj, items)` runs at the top of `specCheck` (`internal/daemon/speccheck.go:130`), so the owner is refused before any spec-check role costs tokens, and again at the top of `startWave` (the authority, before any member is admitted). A blocked item refuses the whole call with code `refused` and the text `S2 waits on S1 (not done); S3 waits on S4 (in this wave, not done)`. A failed read refuses too (fail closed). Nothing is written. The TUI and CLI already show a refusal verbatim.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- TestItemDepsReadsBlockedBy (slicercli): `slicer deps S2 --json --lean --root R` with `{"id":"S2","blocked_by":["S1"]}` decodes `BlockedBy`; the lean `{"id":"S2"}` decodes to empty lists.
- TestWaveStartRefusesABlockedItem (daemon): S1 clean and S2 with `blocked_by: ["S9"]` gives code `refused` naming `S2` and `S9`, no run record is written for either item (S1 is not admitted), and no spec-check role runs.
- TestWaveStartNamesABlockerInTheSameWave (daemon): S2 blocked by S1 with both in the wave is refused with `in this wave`.
- TestWaveStartAllowsItemsWithNoBlockers (daemon): the existing admission tests still pass with the default `deps` route (empty `blocked_by`); two clean items start.
- TestWaveStartRefusesWhenTheDepsReadFails (daemon): a failing `slicer deps` refuses with its error and writes nothing.
- TestSpecCheckRefusesABlockedItemBeforeAnyRole (daemon): `spec.check` on a blocked item is `refused` and the runner is never called (the fake runner fails the test if it runs).
- TestWaveStartPrintsTheBlockedRefusal (cli): with the daemon call stubbed to return the refusal, `ork wave start` exits with failure, prints the text and its code once, and never reaches `Start this wave?`.
- TestWavesLaunchShowsTheBlockedRefusal (tui): `l` with a ticked blocked item shows the daemon's text in the status line, starts nothing, and keeps the items ticked.
- TestWavesStartRefusalKeepsTheTicks (tui): a `wave.start` that returns the refusal (a block that appeared after the check) shows the text and leaves the items ticked and the view open.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
UI slice: UI pass (r14), for the refusal text on the status line and `docs/dashboard.md`. Independent of S166 and S167; if S167 lands first its single-slice launch passes through `specCheck` and so inherits the refusal (see Open 2).
1. Tests first. Add a default route to `runDaemon` (`internal/daemon/runs_test.go:51-68`): `clitest.Route{Tool: "slicer", Args: []string{"deps"}, Prefix: true, Stdout: `{"id":"S1"}`}` so existing wave and spec-check tests keep their meaning. A test that needs a blocker passes its own route first (`append(routes, ...)` puts caller routes first).
2. `internal/slicercli/types.go`: `ItemDeps{ID string; WaitsOn, BlockedBy, Dependents []string}` with the JSON names slicer prints. `slicercli.go`: `ItemDeps(ctx, root, id)` beside `Deps` (:58), running `deps ID --json --lean --root ROOT`.
3. `internal/daemon/build.go` (next to `EngineConflict`, :66): `BlockedMessage` formats `S2 waits on S1 (not done)`, adding `in this wave, ` when the blocker is another item of the call; items in the order given, blockers in slicer's order.
4. `internal/daemon/runs.go`: `func (d *Daemon) blockedItems(ctx, proj registry.Project, ids []string) error` calls `ItemDeps` per distinct id and returns `&ipc.Error{Code: CodeRefused, Message: BlockedMessage(...)}` when any `BlockedBy` is non-empty; a read error is returned as is.
5. `startWave` (:597): call it after the item checks at :600-607, before the Files inspection, for one or more items (the engine-conflict loop at :610-632 runs only for two or more). `specCheck` (`speccheck.go:130`): call it after `d.registered` (:150) and before any `ShowRaw` or role call.
6. TUI and CLI: no new code expected. `applyWaves` shows an error from `kind == "start"` and the spec-check path shows its error through `actionError` (`internal/tui/model.go:1483`), which prints a `refused` message alone. Confirm that in the TUI tests; fix only what they show.
7. Docs: `design.md:162-200` (Check step: dependencies are read first), `dashboard.md:1060-1100` (the refusal), `CHANGELOG.md`.
Open: (1) Refuse or warn. Default: refuse the whole call. Alternative: warn on the status line and require a second `l` (more code, and a blocked item may still fail later). (2) Scope: wave start and the spec check only (default), or also `run.plan`/`run.start`, so `ork run` and the Roadmap launch refuse a blocked item too (the Roadmap already lists only ready slices; `ork run PROJECT ID` can name any). (3) Show `<` dependency markers in the Waves rows before launch (default: no; the refusal is enough).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`
- `go vet ./...`
- `gofmt -l .` (must print nothing)
- `go test ./internal/tui -update`, then review the diff in `testdata/golden/`
- `slicer check --root /Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork`
- `adj lint --root /Users/jon/code/squalor-xyz/ork`
